notes: Harker Football Green (3WR). Tuned from the 2025 draft in this same league, where the top four finishers all had their tight end by round 6 and the champion took only one receiver in six rounds. Sample is one season and twelve managers, so these are nudges, not laws.

rules.label: RB-RB start
rules.note: Still the right open here. This league over-drafts receivers — 63 of 180 picks in 2025 — which is exactly what leaves running back value on the table.

rules.label: Tight end by round 6
rules.note: The strongest signal in the 2025 draft. Every top-four finisher had their TE between rounds 3 and 6; you took yours in round 9 and finished 5th. Round 2 was too early — the manager who spent two of his first three picks on tight ends missed the playoffs entirely.

rules.label: Four skill picks, no TE
rules.note: Four running backs and receivers through five rounds with the tight end slot still empty is the shape that finished 5th and 6th last year. Take the tight end.

rules.label: QB after the top two
rules.note: No timing signal in the 2025 data — the champion took his quarterback in round 4 and the runner-up in round 8, and both made the final. So this stays a pure price preference: not Josh Allen or Lamar Jackson at their cost.
